sources.entry: µStreamer - Lightweight and very quick server to stream MJPEG video from any V4L2 device to the net. GPL-3.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: µStreamer is a lightweight, fast server that streams MJPEG video from V4L2 capture devices over the network, part of the PiKVM project.
summary.what_it_does: µStreamer captures video from any V4L2 device and serves it as an MJPEG stream over HTTP that browsers and common video players can open. It encodes JPEG frames using multiple threads and can use hardware M2M encoding on Raspberry Pi. It can keep showing a "NO LIVE VIDEO" black screen when the device disconnects and reconnects once it is back. Options include DV-timings for resolution changes from the source signal, dropping identical frames to save bandwidth on static HDMI input, streaming over a UNIX domain socket, and systemd socket activation. It also offers GPIO stream-state signaling via libgpiod, an optional built-in file server, and an optional H.264/Janus WebRTC integration. The README says it aims to be compatible with mjpg-streamer's API, but it does not expose webcam controls over HTTP the way mjpg-streamer does.
use_cases: stream a webcam over the network in the browser
stream HDMI capture card output with high FPS
serve MJPEG video from V4L2 devices
low-bandwidth streaming of static screen content
remote KVM video streaming on Raspberry Pi
replace mjpg-streamer for high-quality live video
notable: Multithreaded JPEG encoding, with hardware M2M encoding on Raspberry Pi
--drop-same-frames option skips byte-identical frames to cut HDMI streaming traffic
Shows a NO LIVE VIDEO screen on device disconnect instead of stopping the stream
DV-timings support for changing resolution on the fly
caveats: Hardware M2M encoding on Raspberry Pi needs kernel 5.15.32 or newer; OpenMAX and MMAL support were removed
Cross-domain requests are disabled by default since v2.0 and must be enabled with --allow-origin
Does not provide HTTP access to webcam controls such as focus or brightness, unlike mjpg-streamer
